author: Pete Fiutak
title: Oregon State College Football Preview 2026: JaMarcus Shepherd Rebuilds the Beavers - NewsBreak
text:
By Pete Fiutak ,
2 minutes ago It’s hard to find any program that got hit harder by college football expansion and realignment than Oregon State.
It’s up to new head coach JaMarcus Shephard to build the Beavers back up in a new and expanded Pac-12. This is his first time as a head man, there’s almost no continuity in personnel, and he needs time to make the program his.
Oregon State head coach JaMarcus Shephard watches his team warm up before the Oregon State Spring Game at Reser Stadium on Saturday, April 25, 2026, in Corvallis, Ore.© Kevin Neri/Statesman Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images
It’s not like it was a Pac-12 superpower before the world changed, but former head coach Jonathan Smith was on a run of 25 wins in three seasons with three bowl appearances before leaving for Michigan State.
That wasn’t the norm for the program. In 108 years of Oregon State football, there have only been 43 winning seasons, and few runs with three or more straight great seasons.
The Beavers tried to stay competitive over the last two years, but it’s been hard. The transfer portal hasn’t been kind, the NIL side hasn’t been great, and more than anything else, the disrespect by not being brought into the Power Four fold was a killer.
Oregon State is a part of a real conference again. Let the building begin.
Oregon State Quick Hits Head Coach: JaMarcus Shephard (1st year as a head coach) Best Case / Worst Case: Get bowl eligible/A third straight losing season Key Player: Maalik Murphy, QB Sr. 2025 Record: 2-10 Biggest Question: How fast can the Beavers find an identity? - 2026 Oregon State Schedule Analysis
Oregon State Key 2025 Stats Penalties: Opponents 91 for 767 yards, Oregon State 71 for 599 yards First Half Scoring: Opponents 201, Oregon State 83 Fumbles: Oregon State 18 (lost 7), Opponents 12 (lost 1) Offense JaMarcus Shephard is an offensive coach by trade - he was an elite coordinator at several stops. He’s bringing in a few coordinators to help the cause, and his attack is going to throw and keep pressing.
There’s way too much work to do, but the offense will be more effective and efficient.
What’s Working Shephard has his quarterback. The Beavers ended up using three quarterbacks throughout last season, but this is Maalik Murphy’s attack.
The former Texas Longhorn and Duke Blue Devil pressed too much last year, but he has the size, arm, and ability to do a little of everything if he gets a little help.
The staff did a wonderful job bringing in receivers. There was an insane amount of movement at wideout, with 12 players as a part of the portal.
The top three receivers might be gone, but Aaron Butler (Texas), Aeryn Hampton (Alabama), and Xayvion Noland (UT Rio-Grande Valley) will instantly fit.
Big picture, the Beavers just need to close. Scoring was a problem overall, but the fourth quarter was their best - to a point.
They always fought the good fight, but they lost three games by four points or fewer. A little more offensive pop changes the season.
What Needs Work The entire offensive line needs work. It couldn’t come up with a push for the ground game, and the pass protection was spotty. But now there’s no continuity to build off of. The staff went for bigger blockers through the portal, but they might need a while to jell.
Turnovers were a huge problem. They were mostly errors from effort - too much pressing - but the Beavers gave the ball away multiple times in eight games.
Between the turnovers, and problems on third downs, and the late-game stalls, the biggest issue was …
The Beavers were awful in the red zone. Again with the closing. Oregon State came away empty a whopping 11 times when driving inside the 20.
One misfire was in the three-point loss to Houston. Two were in the unforgivable loss to Sam Houston, and there were three red zone trips without points in the four-point loss to App State.
Player to Watch Aaron Butler, WR Soph.
Enough receivers are coming in to play around with the rotation, but one has to stand out from the pack.
Butler was a great recruit for Texas, but he wasn’t able to break through. He needs to be used in a variety of ways as one of the top playmakers.
- Pac-12 Win Total Predictions
Defense The offense had more problems than the defense did last season.
There weren’t enough big takeaways, but considering it didn’t get a ton of help from the other side, the defense did what it could to stay in games.
There might be some big losses, but there’s enough talent back in spots to build something better, and it starts with …
What’s Working Mike MacIntyre is the defensive coordinator. Really? Shephard landed the former head coach at Colorado, FIU, and San Jose State - and a strong assistant at other spots - to handle the defense? He’s the exact type of veteran the coaching staff as a whole needs.
The linebacking corps will be a plus. Aiden Sullivan is back on the inside after making 72 tackles, Dylan Layne was a wonderful get from Idaho, and Jabari Odoemenem is a ready-to-roll veteran coming in from Duquesne.
Third down conversions - the Beavers were wonderful at getting off the field. They gave up plenty of yards, but except when things got out of hand against the elite, there was a lot of bending without breaking. They finished the season allowing teams to convert just 33% of the time on third downs, holding four teams to under 20%.
What Needs Work The defensive line needs talent. For the most part, Oregon State was able to hold serve in the portal at several positions, but not on the D line. 312-pound Tevita Pome’e is back to be an anchor, but the front four lost Thomas Collins to UCF and Jojo Johnson to Texas Tech.
Coming up with more takeaways is a must. The defense has to create its own breaks after recovering just one fumble and forcing nine turnovers overall. It came up with multiple takeaways twice.
The pass rush needs to be better. There was pressure, and the plays in the backfield were there at times, but the sacks were missing. There wasn’t a ton of help from the portal for the edges.
Player to Watch Dylan Layne, LB Sr.
The Idaho transfer is a baller. A beefed-up safety, he turned into a big playmaker last season with 88 stops and plenty of plays in pass coverage, and now he needs to become a statistical star in the Oregon State corps.
Keys to the Season The new coaching staff has to get everything up to speed.
In the new world of college football, there’s no grace period, and the expectations are always there to win right away, but in this case, it’s about building a culture and a style. The idea is to make Oregon State a place that transfers want to see as a destination.
Player Who Needs To Shine AJ Newberry, RB Sr.
Can the new guy from Vanderbilt handle the rushing attack? The Beavers were gutted at running back, losing star Anthony Hankerson, along with new Iowa State Cyclone Salahadin Allah. Newberry wasn’t used much with the Commodores, but he’s about to get his shot.
Biggest Concern Both lines.
The skill players should be okay in time, and the defense overall should be pieced together to be decent. The lines, though, don’t have the depth, and they’re missing the stars to control the narrative.
Biggest Game at Colorado State, October 3
It’s the first game of the rest of Oregon State’s Pac-12 life, and the atmosphere at Colorado State should be jumping. It’s a must-win home date for the Rams, and they’ll come out fired up, but if the Beavers pull this off, there’s a chance to go on a bit of a run with three home games in the next four.
Transfer Portal We’ve tried to sugarcoat it throughout this, and the Beavers did get several good prospects, but they got gutted after the coaching changes.
On the plus side, the guys they did get should fit right away. This is a good coaching staff, and talent evaluation should be the key here.
Best Signing Broderick Shull, OT (Auburn)
There was a plan with the transfer portal signings. Of course, get the best players possible, but more than anything else, bulk up. Both lines needed to get stronger, bigger, and more bruising.
Here comes the 6-6, 331-pound Shull from Auburn. A redshirt freshman, he’ll have time to grow into one of the leaders up front.
Biggest Loss Jacob Strand, OT (Auburn)
The Beavers lost their starting left tackle to the SEC team - and it sort of reflects the two styles.
Auburn wants quicker linemen who can move in the fast offense, and it took Oregon State’s guy who can be that. The Beavers want bigger linemen, and Shull fits.
Other Names to Know Braden Atkinson QB (Mercer) Daniel Matagi, DT (Portland State) Isaiah Houi, CB (Eastern Illinois) CFN Season Prediction Last year’s team was weird.
It should’ve beaten a good Houston team, but lost to a mediocre App State squad the next week. It pulled off a shocker against Washington State, and whiffed against Sam Houston a week later.
It was a 2-10 team that really should’ve been around 5-7, but it lost its way.
Now there’s a direction. There’s a new coaching staff, a better conference, and now the rebuilding can begin. It’ll take a little while.
CFN Prediction: 5-7
This season will be more like 2024 than 2025. The defense struggled in both seasons, but the offense was better two years ago, especially against the mediocre.
The difference will be a revamped attack that might not be consistent, but will find a way to put up enough points in a few random games to work its way to five victories.
And next year, things will start to get a little easier.
